discussion_comments.comment_body:
(I noticed containerd has been actually unsharing a cgroup namespace per a container, not per a pod. Do we need to keep this ~bug (?)~ ~for compatibility~? ~My opinion is not.~)

https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/v2.4.1/internal/cri/server/container_create.go#L765-L771

CRI-O seems to have been correctly unsharing it per a ~pod~ container
https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/blob/v1.37.1/server/container_create.go#L971
(`createSandboxContainer` in CRI-O is called per a container, not per a pod (❗))

> [!NOTE]
> **EDIT**: Initially I was planning to unshare the cgroup namespace per a pod. On the second thought, now I think we should follow the current behavior of containerd and CRI-O (i.e., per a container). Unsharing it per a pod doesn't make much sense as each of containers has their own cgroup. Submitted an amendment:
> - https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6462

Making -1 mean two different things is prone to confusing users and is going to be hard to document in a way users have good visibility into.

If "nofile" doesn't support unlimited, should we allow -1 for "nofile" at all? Or are we trying to express "1048576" as *effectively* being the same as unlimited?

EDIT: I checked and the kernel does support unlimited for "nofile".  So I'm guessing were making a policy decision here.  How about we handle unlimited uniformly on all ulimits and instead enforce policy either via validation or clamping?
You're right, `nofile` should be consistent with other RLIMITs. I'll add the necessary constraints to the kube-apiserver validation logic; this was indeed an oversight. Thanks for pointing it out!
